author: reek
body: Runtime coverage for the hex wargame engine. Every one of the thirteen scenarios is played to its conclusion and its result printed, so the turn loop, the combat resolution, the retreat paths and the victory scoring all execute rather than merely compiling.

author: reek
body: The engine had no runtime test at all until the tail-call shuffle miscompile was found, and hexwar-loop was the function that miscompiled: its fifth parameter was assigned its fourth argument, the player alternation stopped, and the turn counter never reached the limit. Every scenario below hung. A compile-only check could not see any of it, which is the reason this file exists rather than a note saying the engine builds.

author: reek
body: The engine is deterministic -- each scenario is seeded explicitly -- so the turn counts and the winners are stable and are pinned in the expected output.

author: reek
body: What this pins is that every scenario reaches its own turn limit: the counts below are 10, 12, 15, 16, 18, 20 and 25, each matching the turn-limit its config declares, and it is precisely that advance the miscompile destroyed. Read it as nothing more.

author: reek
body: What it does NOT pin, and what the reader should not take from a green run: every scenario ends winner=Draw with A-lost=0, B-lost=0 and both victory-point totals zero. No unit is eliminated and no objective is scored in any of the thirteen. That is uniform across seeds and maps, which is the signature of combat resolution never firing rather than of thirteen genuine stalemates. It is recorded in the register as an open question about the engine and is deliberately not chased here -- but a golden of identical rows would otherwise read as proof the combat model works, and it is not that.
